text:
alex_k: Quick check — can we agree on a single canonical source for quant profiles? Right now runtime, ops, and model-steering diverge. Need a lightweight checklist before the next canary.

tara: +1. What do you mean by canonical? a single protobuf in git + CI, or just an S3 manifest? :thinking:

liam: I'm leaning git-backed signed releases for authoring + audit. Ops wants an S3 artifact for runtime efficiency. Both can work if we have a canonical build step.

alex_k: Proposal: author in git (proto + tests + sample prompts). CI builds a signed artifact bundle and uploads to S3 with deterministic name (model+profile+sha). Runtime reads manifest from S3 but verifies signature/hash against the git tag. That gives UX + runtime perf.

tara: Distribution solved. Observability: we need explicit profile metadata fields: expected_quality_delta, calibration_dataset_hash, sample_prompts, and a quick-visibility tag for canary cohorts.

jia: Add a compatibility_mask too — a list of ops or runtime flags that are known-incompatible (e.g., certain grouped matmul layouts). Runtime must refuse to apply incompatible profiles for a given hardware path.

liam: Implementation detail: runtime decision must be O(1). Can we do a tiny preflight: model_uuid + profile_hash -> signature check -> compatibility table lookup. If fails, instant fallback to safe FP16 path. No long reconciliation.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline note: Canary flow recommended: shadow-apply -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with rollback triggers bound to quality and infra signals. Documented in /runbooks/quant-canary.md.

alex_k: On detection, let's define "quality_regression" concretely: either baseline log-likelihood delta > 0.02 on the calibration set OR human-reviewed failure rate > 1% for the canary traffic. Keep thresholds adjustable per-customer.

tara: Good starting point. Important: detection != enforcement. First step: automated alerting + annotated traces. Only then apply automated rollback if strict safety gates trip (latency or memory regressions).

liam: For enforcement gates: auto-fallback if latency delta > 30% or memory increase > 20% vs baseline. Cost-only regressions should create billing alerts but not auto-rollback.

alex_k: API contract idea: runtime exposes /profiles/{model}/{version}/meta returning flat metadata: name, hash, expected_quality_delta, ops_blacklist, calibration_hash, created_by, release_tag. Keep the payload tiny, strings and arrays only.

jia: Note for Private/VPC/on-prem installs: runtime might not be allowed to contact S3. Include signed tarball with the release artifact so operators can stage locally and runtime verifies signature before applying.

tara: Can we drop a small example profile snippet for clarity?

alex_k: ```
name: "quant-v2-smallprompt"
hash: "sha256:abc123"
expected_quality_delta: "0.015"
ops_blacklist: ["fused_conv_grouped"]
calibration_hash: "sha1:deadbeef"
release_tag: "canary-2026-03-21"
```

liam: Slight nit: ops_blacklist should be normalized strings (no nested objects) so runtime checks are cheap. Also we should include a tiny compiled-compat bitmap for older runtimes to avoid parsing overhead.

alex_k: Agreed. Final asks: someone draft the short RFC that captures artifact lifecycle + API contract + observability signals. Ops: can you draft distribution/runbook? Runtime: I'll draft the runtime change set.

tara: I'll start the runbook this afternoon and put a PR in ops-runbooks. @alex_k can you aim to have the RFC by EOD Friday?

alex_k: Yep — I can draft the RFC and include a small validation harness (unit tests + sample calset). Will ping for reviews. :thumbsup:

liam: Happy to review runtime bits. If we declare signed artifacts and manifest schema today, I can prototype the quick preflight.

jia: I'll add a ticket for compatibility_mask canonicalization and a task to generate the per-hardware quick-compat bitmaps.

ops-bot: action items created: #PROF-412 (RFC), #OPS-239 (runbook), #RT-678 (runtime preflight).

alex_k: Thanks all — sync up in the RFC PR.
